problem: "Coarse frequency gives the metre range" is confusing and close to reversed: the coarse (low) modulation frequency gives the long unambiguous range and resolves the whole cycles N, while the fine (high) frequency gives the fine reading. A student can read "metre range" as maximum range in metres.
fix: Write: the high (fine) frequency gives the fine resolution, about a millimetre or less; the low (coarse) frequency gives the long unambiguous range and settles the whole number of cycles N.

problem: The sentence "λ = v/f is the modulation wavelength in air" repeats the meaning already given in the term list under the formula, so the reader meets the same definition twice in three lines.
fix: Delete the repeated sentence and keep only the two uses of the two frequencies: fine frequency for resolution, coarse frequency for the long unambiguous range.

problem: "Target plate: helps aim in reflectorless mode" is vague and slightly misleading. A target plate or reflective sheet is a physical surface fixed on the object so the beam returns well where the natural surface is poor, and plates with printed patterns are also used for aiming in prism work.
fix: Write: a target plate or reflective sheet gives a clean, well-defined return surface where the object itself reflects poorly (dark, wet or rough surfaces); with a prism it also gives a clear aiming mark.
